newsitem.title: USA: S. Carolina has record $5.7 bln capital investment.
newsitem.headline: S. Carolina has record $5.7 bln capital investment.

text.p: South Carolina saw its best economic development ever in 1996, with $5.7 billion in capital investment by businesses and nearly 26,000 new jobs, Gov. David Beasley said.
It was only the second time since 1988 the state topped the $3 billion mark for capital investment by businesses, the governor said Thursday at a series of news conferences throughout the state.
Beasley said the average salary for newly created jobs in 1996 was $30,211, compared with an average salary of $23,298 for all jobs statewide.
Beasley attributed much of the economic development to the Enterprise Zone Act passed in 1995 and the Rural Development Act approved in 1996.
The laws classified nearly 90 percent of the state as enterprise zones and allowed county governments to offer tax breaks to new and existing industries.
Beasley said $1.7 billion was invested in 1996 by 429 firms in rural South Carolina, which led to 8,479 new jobs.
